newsitem.title: USA: ITT stock falls on earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: ITT stock falls on earnings warning.

text.p: The stock of ITT Corp. fell Tuesday after the hotel and casino owner said its third-quarter profits would be flat due to weak gambling results.
ITT was down $8 at $48.00 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said late Monday that its gambling operation had been hurt by construction delays at the Caesars Palace casino in Las Vegas and construction disruptions at the Desert Inn casino.
The poor showing also stemmed from increased competition in the Tunica, Miss., gambling market, ITT said.
ITT, which also owns Sheraton hotels and Madison Square Garden in New York, said its other businesses did well in the latest quarter.
Wall Street had expected ITT to post third-quarter earnings equal to about 82 cents a share and profits for the year of $2.61 a share.

Jason Ader, an analyst at Bear Stearns, said the brokerage house lowered its third-quarter earnings estimate for ITT to 56 cents a share from 84 cents and its fourth-quarter estimate to 76 cents a share from 78 cents. It also cut its full-year forecast to $2.30 a share from $2.60.
"The main reason for the earnings shortfall was that baccarat revenues in Las Vegas weere down sharply," Ader said.
"It is important to note that this is not a Las Vegas gaming market problem. Baccarat results at Mirage Resorts Inc. and MGM Grand Inc. are very strong," he said.
Ader said the firm lowered its earnings estimates for ITT mainly because of "the liklihood of significant construction disruption through the end of 1997 in Las Vegas and Atlantic City."
